summary: A short label that appears on hover and keyboard focus. It names icon buttons and reveals truncated text for sighted users; the accessible name always lives on the trigger.
whenToUse: Every IconButton, with the same text as its label.
Truncated text, to show the full value.
Wrap the app once in TooltipProvider so neighbouring tooltips open instantly after the first one.

Plain-script pages without React put tooltipAttributes() from @bridge-ds/react/dom on the trigger and call bindTooltips() once: the same tooltip, delay and keyboard behavior. Never a homemade data-tip tooltip: the design system audit counts those as look-alikes.
whenNotToUse: Information users need to complete a task: show it inline or in a Popover. Tooltips are invisible on touch screens.
Interactive content (links, buttons): tooltips cannot be reached. Use Popover.
Repeating a visible label: it adds noise.

dos.title: Match the trigger's label
dos.text: IconButton label="Copy token name" and the tooltip "Copy token name": what users see and hear is the same.

donts.title: Tooltips on disabled buttons to explain why
donts.text: Disabled buttons do not receive focus, so keyboard users never see it. Explain inline instead.

accessibility: Base UI treats tooltips as visual labels: the trigger must carry the accessible name (IconButton label), which screen readers announce. The popup is not announced.
Opens on hover after the provider delay (500ms) and immediately on keyboard focus; Escape dismisses it.
The trigger must be focusable: wrap a Button, IconButton or Link, never plain text.
Inverse surface (tooltip.bg, tooltip.text) passes 4.5:1 in both themes.
contentGuidelines: A few words, sentence case, no period.
For icon buttons: the action ("Delete token"), not the icon name ("Trash").
Keyboard shortcuts can follow the label: "Copy token name (C)".
